objective: Assess repair commit 3ddedda of the Pi extension entry (range b7efd82..3ddedda, worktree /home/user/holyagent-0.3.0-ext) for security regressions, focusing on the new --project argument and process.chdir in the pi bundle entry and the neutral exec cwd.
scope: The earlier security review found no blocker and one low suspicion: pi.exec of bare sh and git with cwd set to the project could resolve a program from the project folder on Windows. The repair runs sh and git in the package folder, passes git -C <project>, and adds a leading --project <dir> to the pi bundle (packages/runtime/src/hooks/pi-entry.ts, pi-project.ts) which chdirs before the CLI runs. It also shares hasStateFolder (hooks/state-folder.ts) and a bundler (packages/runtime/src/bundle.ts).
Diff without dist: /home/user/holyagent-notes/pi-ext-fix.diff; read worktree files as needed.
constraints: Read-only: no edits and no version-control writes.
Report in under 350 words; start each evidence line with the criterion text, a colon, then the support.

criteria.text: The --project argument cannot be confused with an option or used to run the CLI against an unintended folder, and a missing folder fails closed
sh and git no longer start in the project folder, and no new command, path or context injection is introduced

notes:
- Low, hardening: the extension passes `ctx.cwd` to `--project` and `git -C` as-is. If a host ever gave a relative `ctx.cwd`, `chdir` would resolve it against the package folder instead of the project. That fails closed unless a same-named subfolder exists there. Pi's `ctx.cwd` is absolute, so this is theoretical. `resolve(ctx.cwd)` in `collect` would remove it.
- Pre-existing and unchanged: `git -C <project>` and the CLI after `chdir` read the project's own git config and `.holyagent/config.json`. That is the same trust as launching Pi in that repo, and git's `safe.directory` check still applies.
- Pre-existing and out of scope: the CLI spawns its own children with the project as cwd. The Claude plugin does the same.

evidence:
- The --project argument cannot be confused with an option or used to run the CLI against an unintended folder, and a missing folder fails closed:
  - `projectOf` in `pi-project.ts` only reads a leading `--project` plus `args[1]` as one separate argv element. A dash-prefixed folder name is still just the directory, and `chdir` parses no options. In the wrapper (`claude/src/wrapper.sh:42`), `exec bun … holyagent.js "$@"` puts the arguments after the script file, so Bun does not parse them.
  - A bare `--project` or a non-leading one is left in place, so the CLI rejects it as an unknown command. The Claude plugin bundle has no such flag.
  - `enterProject` (`pi-entry.ts:967-971`) turns a failed `chdir` (ENOENT, ENOTDIR, empty string) into `StateIo`. `pi-entry.ts:1011-1013` writes the error, sets a nonzero exit code and never reaches `config` or the CLI. The extension also requires exit code 0. A test covers the missing-folder case (exit code 4).
  - `main.ts` is imported only after `chdir` and reads `process.cwd()` at run time (`cli/main.ts:38`). `Bun.argv.splice(2,2)` strips exactly the flag and its folder.
- sh and git no longer start in the project folder, and no new command, path or context injection is introduced:
  - `exec` in `extension.ts` always uses `cwd: packageRoot`, which comes from `import.meta.url`.
  - The wrapper is an absolute path as the first operand to `sh`. It never changes directory.
  - Bun now starts in the package folder, so project `.env` and `bunfig.toml` are not read at all.
  - `git -C <project> rev-parse --show-toplevel` is an argv array with no shell, and the project is the value of `-C`.
  - The command strings are fixed: `config`, `status`, `reconcile`, `state mode`. The non-git state folder is `join(top, ".holyagent")`, which is only `stat`-ed.
  - `bundleModule` (`bundle.ts`) is build-time only, with repo-constant entrypoints.
- diff-file: `/home/user/holyagent-notes/pi-ext-fix.diff`

acceptance.rationale: The project flag fails closed and is not parsed as an option; sh and git start in the package folder; no new injection
